lanes.title: Environment: bring the shared foundation up and down

steps.name: Cluster lifecycle
steps.description: Bring the shared foundation up (Kind cluster, in-cluster registry, signed foundation artifacts, Flux bootstrap, and reconciliation) or tear it down. Demo workloads remain inactive until their explicit demo startup command. These serialize: only one lifecycle action runs at a time so destructive operations never overlap.

actions.label: Bring the shared foundation up (make up)

steps.name: Olly Sentinel + ADK
steps.description: Run the enrichment loop end to end, run the ADK eval (signal-check gate + rca_readiness), launch adk web for ADK Studio, and wire ServiceNow / LLM secrets from .env.

lanes.title: Deliver: signed artifacts to running clusters

steps.name: Source and CI
steps.description: Manifests and app code live in git. On merge to main, GitHub Actions packages each component as an OCI artifact and builds the app images with SBOM and provenance. Locally, make push-local performs the identical publish against the in-cluster registry.

steps.name: OCI registry (zot / GHCR)
steps.description: Every input to the cluster is an OCI artifact: manifests, images, signatures. Locally this is zot running in-cluster; in CI-published mode it is GHCR. Signatures travel with the artifacts.

steps.name: Flux verification and reconciliation
steps.description: Flux pulls the artifacts, verifies the cosign signature (keyless OIDC identity in CI mode, the local key pair in local mode) before reconciling, and converges cluster state. Nothing unsigned reaches the cluster.

steps.name: Admission policies
steps.owner: Security team authors, platform team enforces
steps.description: A CEL ValidatingAdmissionPolicy restricts every tenant Flux source to an allowlist, so a compromised tenant cannot point the cluster at an arbitrary registry. Witness policy verification at admission time lands in stage 4.

steps.name: Ingestion queue (purl intake)
steps.description: Third-party packages enter as purls on a NATS JetStream queue. The purl worker checks the cache and queues an isolated install and analysis for anything new.

steps.name: Analysis worker (SBOM under witness)
steps.description: The worker installs the package in an isolated directory and generates an SPDX SBOM with syft. The SBOM step runs under witness run, producing a signed in-toto attestation, and publishes results back to the queue.

steps.name: Archivista evidence store
steps.description: Signed attestations from every witness run land here: SBOM generation, test evidence, VEX analysis. Anything a policy decision later relies on is queryable by anyone with access, across teams.

actions.label: Run tests under witness (evidence to Archivista)

steps.name: Results archive (PostgreSQL)
steps.description: Task results, full SBOM documents, and attestation signatures are archived relationally for reporting and the KPI dashboards.

actions.label: Show recent task results
command: SELECT task_id, status, result_type, archived_at FROM task_results ORDER BY archived_at DESC LIMIT 10;

steps.name: Scan and VEX triage
steps.description: grype scans the stored SBOMs; the VA sub-team triages findings into signed OpenVEX statements: a shared base image CVE, a govulncheck-proven unreachable finding, and an inline-mitigation record. The rescan with VEX applied goes green for the triaged findings.

actions.label: Run the full VEX triage demo

steps.name: Attested VEX retrieval
steps.description: Downstream consumers fetch the merged, attested VEX from Archivista and feed it to their own scanners, so one triage decision is reused everywhere.

steps.name: End-to-end verification
steps.description: The bats suite drives the whole pipeline: publish a task, watch it process, verify SBOM generation, witness attestation, and archival, straight from the cluster.

steps.name: Policy gates (promotion and admission)
steps.owner: Security team authors, platform team enforces
steps.description: A signed witness policy gates promotion: artifacts with attested pipeline evidence pass, tampered ones fail closed, and both decisions land in Archivista. At the cluster boundary, Kyverno denies any pod whose image lacks a valid cosign signature. The revocation walkthrough shows trust being withdrawn and restored end to end.

actions.label: Promotion gate: approve one, reject one

steps.name: Agentic remediation (human in the loop)
steps.description: A sandboxed agent (nono, kernel-enforced) analyzes one CVE against the SBOM, VEX, and reachability evidence and produces a structured recommendation. It stops at the human gate; applying the change requires an explicit approval and lands as a PR branch, with every step witness-attested. Needs nono and the claude CLI on a Linux host; guardrails are in agent/GUARDRAILS.md.
